author: human
request:
Bug report: opening /owners?page=0 — or any page value below 1 — renders the
error page instead of the owner list. Expected behavior: the owner listing
treats any page value below 1 as the first page and responds with the normal
listing (HTTP 200). Find the cause, fix it, and cover the fix with a test.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Owner listing treats a page number below 1 as the first page
summary: Opening the owner listing with a page value below 1 (for example /owners?page=0) renders the error page today. The listing must treat any page value below 1 as the first page and respond with the normal listing.
acceptance_criteria: Given more owners than fit on one page, when the owner listing is requested with page 0, then the response is HTTP 200 and shows the same first page of owners as a request for page 1, not the error page.

Given more owners than fit on one page, when the owner listing is requested with a negative page value, then the response is HTTP 200 and shows the same first page of owners as a request for page 1, not the error page.
Given a page value of 1 or above, or no page value, when the owner listing is requested, then the listing behaves exactly as before this slice.
non_goals: Page handling in the veterinarian directory: the request names only the owner listing.
Non-numeric page values and page values beyond the last page: the request names only values below 1.
notes: Intake line 1 carries the request only (decisions: []); the request itself states the expected behavior, and no Non-Goals row or existing requirement conflicts with it, so no consultation was needed. The request asks for the cause: the controller passes the raw page value into the paging request, and a page index below zero is rejected, which surfaces as the error page. Confirming this is the implementer's job. One data-driven test covers page 0 and a negative page. The PRD adds REQ-OWN-005 to the Owner records narrative with one Done-when bullet; no Non-Goals row changed. No new ubiquitous-language term was needed.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Covered by architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row: normalizing a request parameter to its permitted range is binding, not a business rule, so the clamp belongs in OwnerController's listing handler. The existing-deviation note (§ Pattern Catalog, paragraph after the table) does not apply, because a parameter's range belongs to the request that carries it. The listing contract is the OwnerController row in system-design § Contracts, which now also names REQ-OWN-005. Basis: grep, not the IDE oracle (not connected). OwnerController.processFindForm binds page as a primitive with default 1. findPaginatedForOwnersLastName passes page - 1 straight into PageRequest.of, which rejects a negative index; that exception reaches the error page. No repository, template, or domain type changes.
integration_points: Framework transport: MockMvc drives the real MVC dispatch and request-parameter binding (the one sanctioned mock, per CLAUDE.md § Testing Strategy). Exercise the parameter as an HTTP query value (page=0 and a negative value), not by calling the handler directly.

Repository boundary: reuse the @MockitoBean OwnerRepository fixture OwnerControllerTests already declares, stubbing findByLastNameStartingWith to return a multi-owner Page. The @WebMvcTest slice has no JPA context. A hand-written double of a Spring Data JpaRepository would have to implement its whole inherited surface, so the existing framework stub is the cheapest honest double here. Add no new stub beyond this one.

Binding: no new entry point. The existing GET /owners handler keeps its binding targets unchanged: page as a request-scoped primitive, and the Owner model attribute under the controller's existing @InitBinder id disallow. The slice only clamps the bound page value.

patterns.description: GET /owners handler: normalize page once, at handler entry, before any use of it
pagination helper that converts the 1-based page into the 0-based PageRequest index

risks.risk: The raw page value feeds two places: the PageRequest index and the currentPage model attribute that ownersList renders. Clamping only the query would still render page 0 as current, so the response would differ from page 1.
risks.mitigation: Clamp once at handler entry and pass the clamped value to both the query and addPaginationModel. The acceptance criterion 'same first page as page 1' is then true for the model as well as the query (architecture-principles § Pattern Catalog, Web controller row).

risks.risk: Computing page - 1 before clamping overflows for Integer.MIN_VALUE and wraps to a large positive index.
risks.mitigation: Clamp the 1-based value to a minimum of 1 before the subtraction, so the subtraction never sees an out-of-range operand (security-principles: validate input at the boundary where it enters).

risks.risk: Paged owner listing is a data-scaling path. system-design.md has no Scale and Load section, so no row can be cited.
risks.mitigation: The slice adds no path and changes no query shape: the listing stays one bounded page query plus its count. Simplest readable form.

notes: No design-doc-autofix records in the log; autofix audit skipped. Out of scope per the prd-entry non-goals: VetController's paging helper has the same unclamped shape, and non-numeric page values are also excluded. Brief observation for the owner: docs/system-design.md carries no Scale and Load section. This slice does not need one because it adds no data-scaling path, but a later slice that adds such a path will have to create the section.

author: feature-implementer
error_output: Progress, not a gate failure. The new test compiles and fails as intended; the other 15 OwnerControllerTests and the rest of the suite pass. Cause confirmed: page 0 and -1 raise IllegalArgumentException 'Page index must not be less than zero' from PageRequest.of(page - 1, 5) in OwnerController.findPaginatedForOwnersLastName (wrapped in ServletException). Integer.MIN_VALUE wraps page - 1 to a large positive index, so the page-index-0 stub does not match. Edited: src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/owner/OwnerControllerTests.java (new constants FIRST_PAGE, FIRST_PAGE_INDEX, PAGE_ZERO, A_NEGATIVE_PAGE; factories anOwner() and aFirstPageOfMoreOwnersThanFit(List<Owner>); new @ParameterizedTest with imports ParameterizedTest, ValueSource, PageRequest, argThat). Plan: .scratch/implementation-plan.md. Remaining: Green, which clamps page once at handler entry in OwnerController.processFindForm (int currentPage = Math.max(page, 1), before any subtraction) and passes the clamped value to both findPaginatedForOwnersLastName and addPaginationModel. Then Refactor, the self-review walk (coverage-map and conventions-map; AC3 'page >= 1 or absent behaves as before' is expected to be carried by existing tests such as processFindFormSuccess, check the map), and the full quality gate: build, test, checkFormat/format, checkstyle, handoff validate, audit-autofix, contracts-sync. No production code changed yet.

author: change-grader
summary: clamp owner-listing page below 1 to the first page

blast_radius.note: One production file in one module: a new constant plus a single Math.max clamp in OwnerController.processFindForm, with two call sites switched to the clamped value. The other changes are one parameterized test and matching one-line edits to the PRD and the system-design contract row. No sensitive or security-surface paths.

semantic_surprise.note: Math.max(page, 1) returns the same value for every page of 1 or more, so existing paging is unchanged. The clamped value feeds both the PageRequest index and the currentPage model attribute, so ownersList.html's prev/first links render the same as for page 1. The clamp runs before page - 1, so Integer.MIN_VALUE no longer wraps around. The empty-result and single-owner redirect branches are untouched.

test_adequacy.note: The build passed. The parameterized MockMvc test covers 0, -1 and Integer.MIN_VALUE and asserts status, view, currentPage=1 and the full listOwners. Its stub matches only page index 0, and the setup stub is keyed to 'Franklin', so an unclamped run either throws from PageRequest.of or gets a null page. Either way it fails, so the test is not tautological. Existing page=1 tests cover the unchanged path.

reviewer_hedging.note: All three reviewers on the planned roster approved in the first round with no findings. The security reviewer was scoped out by the plan, which is expected. The citations I checked resolve: architecture-principles.md:85, testing-principles.md:54 and OwnerController.java:131. The test-reviewer's recommendations are first-round polish (drop the redundant -1 row) and a disclaimer about other requirements' edge cases, not worries about this change.

The diff stays on GET /owners as the prd-entry names it. VetController's identical unclamped paging was left alone, as the recorded non-goal says.
